1	# 2024 JavaScript Rising Stars: Top Projects and Ecosystem Shifts
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://risingstars.js.org/2024/en
     5	
     6	This is the 9th edition of JavaScript Rising Stars, analyzing GitHub stars added over the last 12 months for projects curated by Best of JS.
     7	
     8	## Top 10 Most Popular Projects Overall
     9	
    10	The following table shows the projects that gained the most GitHub stars in 2024:
    11	
    12	| Rank | Project | Description | Stars Added |
    13	|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
    14	| 1 | shadcn/ui | Beautifully designed copy-paste components | +38.0k |
    15	| 2 | Excalidraw | Virtual whiteboard for hand-drawn diagrams | +27.0k |
    16	| 3 | AFFiNE | Knowledge base combining Notion + Miro capabilities | +19.6k |
    17	| 4 | Bruno | Open-source API testing IDE (Postman alternative) | +18.7k |
    18	| 5 | n8n | Fair-code workflow automation with native AI | +17.0k |
    19	| 6 | htmx | Access AJAX, WebSockets directly in HTML | +16.8k |
    20	| 7 | Tauri | Desktop/mobile apps with web frontend | +15.9k |
    21	| 8 | Supabase | Open-source Firebase alternative | +14.5k |
    22	| 9 | Flowise | Drag & drop UI for custom LLM flows | +14.5k |
    23	| 10 | Payload | Open-source fullstack Next.js framework | +14.4k |
    24	
    25	## shadcn/ui: Back-to-Back Champion
    26	
    27	shadcn/ui won for the second consecutive year. Its total stars reached 77.5k (created January 2023). The project gained 39.5k stars in 2023 and 38.0k in 2024, sustaining extraordinary momentum.
    28	
    29	![shadcn/ui yearly star trend showing N/A from 2016-2022, 39.5k in 2023, 38.0k in 2024](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    30	
    31	![shadcn/ui monthly trend in 2024 showing January peak at 7.3k, with steady 2-3k monthly additions throughout the year](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    32	
    33	Key 2024 additions include: Charts (powered by Recharts), Themes (CSS variable generation), Blocks (layout collections for typical web apps), a new responsive sidebar component, and a significantly upgraded CLI supporting Next.js, Remix, Vite, Laravel, and monorepos. The CLI can now install components, themes, hooks, utils, and dependencies, and supports importing from any compatible "registry," spawning an ecosystem of derivative libraries like Motion-Primitives and Magic UI. Integration with Vercel's v0 service for AI-generated components further boosted adoption.
    34	
    35	## Front-end Frameworks
    36	
    37	| Rank | Framework | Stars Added |
    38	|------|-----------|-------------|
    39	| 1 | htmx | +16.8k |
    40	| 2 | React | +14.2k |
    41	| 3 | Svelte | +6.1k |
    42	| 4 | Vue.js | +5.9k |
    43	| 5 | Angular | +3.5k |
    44	
    45	htmx rose from #2 in 2023 to #1 in 2024. It extends HTML with `hx-*` attributes to enable data fetching and interactivity without writing JavaScript — ideal for server-driven applications and progressive enhancement of static sites.
    46	
    47	React 19 launched in December after three years of development. New features include Server Components, Server Functions, web component (Custom Elements) support, new hooks, and form actions. Robin Wieruch noted that React is evolving from a library into "a specification for frameworks," representing a shift toward a framework-first mindset while still allowing client-only usage. The React Compiler continues development to improve performance and DX.
    48	
    49	Svelte 5 introduced "runes" — an explicit mechanism for declaring reactive state. Svelte holds the highest positive opinion in the State of JS survey results.
    50	
    51	## React and Vue Ecosystems
    52	
    53	**React Ecosystem Top 5:** shadcn/ui (+38.0k), Excalidraw (+27.0k), Payload (+14.4k), Magic UI (+13.2k), Next.js (+12.1k).
    54	
    55	**Vue Ecosystem Top 5:** Nuxt (+6.2k), PrimeVue (+5.4k), Slidev (+4.7k), shadcn-vue (+4.1k), VitePress (+3.7k).
    56	
    57	Vue 3.5 reworked its reactivity system, with the lighter alien-signals approach already landing in the main branch. The flourishing of Vue UI libraries (PrimeVue, shadcn-vue) signals growing ecosystem confidence. Daniel Roe (Nuxt core team lead) highlighted the active release cycle and regular performance improvements.
    58	
    59	## Emerging Themes: AI, Desktop, and Browser Innovation
    60	
    61	AI-adjacent projects dominated: n8n (+17.0k) for workflow automation with native AI, Flowise (+14.5k) for visual LLM flow building, and Supabase (+14.5k) as an open-source backend. Tauri (+15.9k) continued its push for lighter desktop/mobile apps built with web technologies. Browser-based innovation was showcased by PGlite (Postgres via WebAssembly) and WebVM (a virtual machine running entirely in the browser).
    62	
    63	## Key Findings
    64	
    65	- **Component ownership beats imports:** shadcn/ui's model of letting developers own and customize component code proved its staying power for a second year, reaching 77.5k total stars.
    66	- **HTML-first is serious:** htmx overtook React as the #1 front-end framework by stars added, validating server-driven, low-JavaScript architectures.
    67	- **React is becoming a framework spec:** With Server Components and Server Functions in React 19, multiple frameworks (Next.js, Remix, etc.) now interpret React's primitives differently, making React more of a specification than a standalone library.
    68	- **AI integration is table stakes:** Four of the top 10 overall projects (n8n, Flowise, Supabase, AFFiNE) have significant AI capabilities or integrations.
    69	- **Vue's ecosystem maturity:** A wave of high-quality UI libraries and the Vue 3.5 reactivity overhaul signal a confident, maturing Vue ecosystem.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Create presentation with 16:9 aspect ratio
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette
DARK_BG = RgbColor(0x0F, 0x17, 0x2A)       # Deep navy background
ACCENT = RgbColor(0x38, 0xBD, 0xF8)        # Cyan accent
ACCENT2 = RgbColor(0xF7, 0xB9, 0x31)       # Gold accent
TEXT_PRIMARY = RgbColor(0xF0, 0xF4, 0xF8)  # Off-white
TEXT_SECONDARY = RgbColor(0x94, 0xA3, 0xB8) # Muted gray-blue
BAR_COLORS = [
    RgbColor(0x38, 0xBD, 0xF8),  # cyan
    RgbColor(0xF7, 0xB9, 0x31),  # gold
    RgbColor(0x34, 0xD3, 0x99),  # emerald
    RgbColor(0xA7, 0x8B, 0xFA),  # violet
    RgbColor(0xFB, 0x71, 0x85),  # rose
    RgbColor(0x2D, 0xD4, 0xBF),  # teal
    RgbColor(0xF9, 0x73, 0x16),  # orange
    RgbColor(0x60, 0xA5, 0xFA),  # blue
    RgbColor(0xC0, 0xCA, 0x33),  # lime
    RgbColor(0xEC, 0x48, 0x99),  # pink
]

def set_slide_bg(slide, color=DARK_BG):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18, bold=False, color=TEXT_PRIMARY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf

def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=16, color=TEXT_PRIMARY, bullet_color=ACCENT, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return tf

# ===================== SLIDE 1: Title Cover =====================
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
set_slide_bg(slide1)

# Accent bar at top
shape = slide1.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.15))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
shape.line.fill.background()

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.2),
            "2024 JavaScript Rising Stars", font_size=48, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.1), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.8),
            "The Year's Hottest Projects by GitHub Stars", font_size=28, bold=False, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.3), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.0),
            "9th Edition  •  Methodology: GitHub stars added in 2024 from Best of JS curated list",
            font_size=16, color=TEXT_SECONDARY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(6.6), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.5),
            "Audience: Frontend Engineers & Engineering Managers",
            font_size=14, color=TEXT_SECONDARY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ===================== SLIDE 2: Overall Top 10 =====================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide2)

shape = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
shape.line.fill.background()

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "shadcn/ui Leads Overall with +38k Stars, Followed by Excalidraw and AFFiNE",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.85), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "Top 10 most-starred JavaScript projects on GitHub in 2024",
            font_size=14, color=TEXT_SECONDARY)

# Data
top10 = [
    ("shadcn/ui", 38.0),
    ("Excalidraw", 27.0),
    ("AFFiNE", 19.6),
    ("Bruno", 18.7),
    ("n8n", 17.0),
    ("htmx", 16.8),
    ("Tauri", 15.9),
    ("Supabase", 14.5),
    ("Flowise", 14.5),
    ("Payload", 14.4),
]

max_val = 38.0
chart_left = Inches(0.8)
chart_top = Inches(1.4)
chart_width = Inches(11.7)
chart_height = Inches(5.6)
bar_height = chart_height / len(top10) * 0.72
bar_spacing = chart_height / len(top10)

for i, (name, val) in enumerate(top10):
    y = chart_top + i * bar_spacing
    bar_w = (val / max_val) * (chart_width * 0.72)
    # Rank number
    add_textbox(slide2, chart_left, y, Inches(0.4), bar_height, str(i+1),
                font_size=13, bold=True, color=TEXT_SECONDARY, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    # Bar
    bar = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, chart_left + Inches(0.5), y + Inches(0.05), bar_w, bar_height - Inches(0.1))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = BAR_COLORS[i]
    bar.line.fill.background()
    # Project name
    add_textbox(slide2, chart_left + Inches(0.6), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(3.5), bar_height,
                name, font_size=14, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    # Star count
    add_textbox(slide2, chart_left + Inches(0.5) + bar_w + Inches(0.12), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(1.2), bar_height,
                f"+{val}k", font_size=14, bold=True, color=BAR_COLORS[i], align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ===================== SLIDE 3: shadcn/ui Deep Dive =====================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide3)

shape = slide3.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
shape.line.fill.background()

add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "shadcn/ui: Copy-Paste Components Win for the Second Consecutive Year",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)

# Left column: key stats & features
left_x = Inches(0.6)
add_textbox(slide3, left_x, Inches(1.0), Inches(5.8), Inches(0.4),
            "Year-over-Year Growth", font_size=16, bold=True, color=ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide3, left_x, Inches(1.4), Inches(5.8), Inches(0.9),
            "• 2023: +39.5k stars  |  2024: +38.0k stars\n• Total: 77.5k stars (created Jan 2023)",
            font_size=14, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)

add_textbox(slide3, left_x, Inches(2.2), Inches(5.8), Inches(0.4),
            "Key 2024 Additions", font_size=16, bold=True, color=ACCENT)
features = [
    "Charts (powered by Recharts)",
    "Themes (CSS variable generation)",
    "Blocks (layout collections)",
    "Responsive sidebar component",
    "Upgraded CLI: Next.js, Remix, Vite, Laravel, monorepos",
    "Registry ecosystem: Motion-Primitives, Magic UI",
    "Vercel v0 AI-generated component integration"
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide3, left_x, Inches(2.6), Inches(5.8), Inches(3.8), features, font_size=13, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)

# Right column: images
img_left = Inches(6.8)
if os.path.exists("/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg"):
    slide3.shapes.add_picture("/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg", img_left, Inches(1.0), width=Inches(5.8))
if os.path.exists("/app/benchmark/assets/figure_2.jpg"):
    slide3.shapes.add_picture("/app/benchmark/assets/figure_2.jpg", img_left, Inches(4.2), width=Inches(5.8))

# ===================== SLIDE 4: Frontend Frameworks =====================
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide4)

shape = slide4.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
shape.line.fill.background()

add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "htmx Overtakes React as #1 Front-end Framework by Stars Added",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)

frameworks = [
    ("htmx", 16.8),
    ("React", 14.2),
    ("Svelte", 6.1),
    ("Vue.js", 5.9),
    ("Angular", 3.5),
]
max_fw = 16.8
chart_left = Inches(1.0)
chart_top = Inches(1.3)
chart_width = Inches(7.5)
chart_height = Inches(4.8)
bar_h = Inches(0.65)
bar_gap = Inches(0.28)

for i, (name, val) in enumerate(frameworks):
    y = chart_top + i * (bar_h + bar_gap)
    bar_w = (val / max_fw) * chart_width
    # Bar
    bar = slide4.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, chart_left, y, bar_w, bar_h)
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = BAR_COLORS[i]
    bar.line.fill.background()
    # Name inside bar
    add_textbox(slide4, chart_left + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.12), Inches(2.5), bar_h,
                name, font_size=16, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    # Value at end
    add_textbox(slide4, chart_left + bar_w + Inches(0.12), y + Inches(0.12), Inches(1.0), bar_h,
                f"+{val}k", font_size=16, bold=True, color=BAR_COLORS[i], align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Right side insights
insight_x = Inches(9.0)
add_textbox(slide4, insight_x, Inches(1.3), Inches(4.0), Inches(0.4),
            "Why htmx won", font_size=16, bold=True, color=ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide4, insight_x, Inches(1.75), Inches(4.0), Inches(1.6),
            "Extends HTML with hx-* attributes for AJAX & WebSockets—no JS required. Ideal for server-driven apps and progressive enhancement.",
            font_size=13, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)

add_textbox(slide4, insight_x, Inches(3.2), Inches(4.0), Inches(0.4),
            "React 19 Highlights", font_size=16, bold=True, color=ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide4, insight_x, Inches(3.65), Inches(4.0), Inches(2.0),
            "• Server Components & Server Functions\n• Custom Elements support\n• New hooks & form actions\n• React is evolving from a library into a specification for frameworks",
            font_size=13, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)

add_textbox(slide4, insight_x, Inches(5.3), Inches(4.0), Inches(0.8),
            "Svelte 5 introduced 'runes'—explicit reactive state. Highest positive opinion in State of JS survey.",
            font_size=13, color=TEXT_SECONDARY)

# ===================== SLIDE 5: React Ecosystem =====================
slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide5)

shape = slide5.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08))
shape.fill.solid()
shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
shape.line.fill.background()

add_textbox(slide5, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "React Ecosystem: shadcn/ui, Excalidraw, and Payload Dominate",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)

react_eco = [
    ("shadcn/ui", 38.0),
    ("Excalidraw", 27.0),
    ("Payload", 14.4),
    ("Magic UI", 13.2),
    ("Next.js", 12.1),
]
max_re = 38.0
chart_left = Inches(1.0)
chart_top = Inches(1.3)
chart_width = Inches(7.0)
bar_h = Inches(0.6)
bar_gap = Inches(0.25)

for i, (name, val) in enumerate(react_eco):
    y = chart_top + i * (bar_h + bar_gap)
    bar_w = (val / max_re) * chart_width
    bar = slide5.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, chart_left, y, bar_w, bar_h)
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = BAR_COLORS[i]
    bar.line.fill.background()
    add_textbox(slide5, chart_left + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.1), Inches(2.5), bar_h,
                name, font_size=15, bold=True, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    add_textbox(slide5, chart_left + bar_w + Inches(0.12), y + Inches(0.1), Inches(1.0), bar_h,
                f"+{val}k", font_size=15, bold=True, color=BAR_COLORS[i], align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

insight_x = Inches(8.8)
add_textbox(slide5, insight_x, Inches(1.3), Inches(4.2), Inches(0.4),
            "React's Evolution", font_size=16, bold=True, color=ACCENT)
add_textbox(slide5, insight_x, Inches(1.75), Inches(4.2), Inches(2.2),
            "React 19 marks a shift from standalone library to framework specification. Next.js, Remix, and others now interpret React primitives differently—Server Components and Server Functions are becoming the new baseline.",
